name: Atlassian Jira / Confluence Cloud
scope_notes: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

controls.name: User API tokens (authentication policy)
controls.what: Blocks members in a policy from creating new or using existing user API tokens against the org's apps; takes up to 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Block members from creating a new or using an existing API token
controls.quote: By default, your organization's user API token settings are set to allow access. With the user API token setting, you can allow or block members from: Creating a new API token Using an existing API token

controls.name: User API token expiration (authentication policy)
controls.what: Sets user API tokens of policy members to expire after 1-365 days (or never).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Never expires / Expires
controls.quote: You can set the token to never expire or set a different expiration date in an authentication policy. You can set the token to expire between 1 to 365 days.

controls.name: API token access for external users
controls.what: Blocks external (unmanaged) users from calling app APIs with user API tokens, including existing tokens.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > External users > API token access for external users > Block
controls.quote: When you block user API token access for external users, they are unable to use a token to access app s through an app API, even if they previously used a token to access them.

controls.name: Revoke user API tokens
controls.what: Org admins can permanently revoke managed accounts' API tokens, singly or in bulk, or via the Delete API token API.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity > Revoke
controls.quote: You can to revoke one or more of a managed account’s API tokens from one place.

controls.name: IP allowlists
controls.what: Users outside allowed IPs/locations cannot reach Jira/Confluence content, including via the APIs.
controls.setting: admin.atlassian.com > Security > Device security > IP allowlists
controls.plan: Premium (Jira, JSM, Confluence, Compass) or Enterprise (Analytics, Focus)
controls.quote: Users also won't be able to access that app programmatically via the APIs.

controls.name: Block user apps (user-installed apps)
controls.what: Restricts app installation to admins so end users cannot grant third-party (3LO) apps access.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > settings > Block user apps
controls.quote: Organization and Site admins can also choose to restrict app installation to admin level by selecting Block user apps in the Connected apps settings.

controls.name: Uninstall connected app
controls.what: Uninstalling a 3LO app from the site revokes all users' grants.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > Manage authorization > Uninstall
controls.quote: For OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps such as “Atlassian for VS Code” , the Uninstall button revokes all users.

controls.name: Marketplace and custom app access control (data security policy)
controls.what: Blocks eligible installed apps from user-generated content, org-wide or in selected spaces; finer allow-lists need Guard.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > Data protection > Data security policy > Marketplace and custom app access
controls.plan: Any plan to block all; Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium for selective allow
controls.quote: All organization admins are able to use an override to block all eligible Marketplace and custom apps. The override blocks those apps from accessing user-generated content, such as Confluence pages and Jira work item data in their organization.

controls.name: Service account API token expiration
controls.what: Admin picks a 1-365 day expiry when creating a service account API token (default one year).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token
controls.quote: Select an expiration date for the API token. Token expiration can be between 1 and 365 days.

controls.name: Service account API token scopes
controls.what: Token scopes are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token > scopes
controls.quote: Once you create an API token, you can’t modify its scopes. If you want to apply different scopes, you’ll need to create a new token.

controls.name: Revoke service account API token
controls.what: Revoked tokens stop working and are removed, within about 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > credentials > Revoke
controls.quote: When you revoke a token it no longer works and we permanently remove it from your account.

controls.name: Service account OAuth 2.0 credential scopes
controls.what: Admin must select scopes (Jira, Confluence, Goals, Projects only) when creating the client credential.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > OAuth 2.0
controls.quote: OAuth 2.0 credentials for service accounts use scopes by default. The scope for an OAuth 2.0 credential defines the levels of access to data in your Atlassian app s.

controls.name: Revoke service account OAuth 2.0 credential
controls.what: Revoking permanently removes the client credential.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > credentials > Revoke
controls.quote: When you revoke a OAuth 2.0 credential for a service account it no longer works and we permanently remove it from your account.

controls.name: Service account app roles and groups
controls.what: Admins choose which apps/roles and groups a service account has, which bounds what its credentials can reach.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > create/edit > roles, groups
controls.quote: Select roles for the app s that the service account needs to access. You can also add the service account to a group.

controls.name: Delete service account
controls.what: Deleting the account removes all its access and credentials.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > ••• > Delete account
controls.quote: When you delete a service account, this means the service account can no longer access any app s. We also delete the credentials associated with this service account.

controls.name: Create a service account (Organization admin only)
controls.what: Only organization admins can create service accounts and their credentials, so other users cannot mint these credentials.
controls.plan: Atlassian Guard Standard or Enterprise (5 service accounts free)

no_control.what: The Marketplace and custom app access control cannot block apps that use Atlassian API tokens.
no_control.quote: Marketplace, custom and other third-party app s that use Atlassian API tokens to access data

no_control.what: Admins cannot create or issue API tokens on a user's behalf (only users create them).
no_control.quote: It’s not possible for anyone else to create an API token on behalf of a user. Users must create API tokens themselves.

renewal.summary: The static API token is reused on each request until it expires (1 to 365 days); after that the user must create a new token. No refresh token is involved.

authentication.summary: An organization service account gets a client ID and client secret. A script posts them to https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token with grant_type=client_credentials (2LO) and uses the returned bearer access token against api.atlassian.com.

federation.details: The documented flow exchanges a stored client secret for an access token. The page does not describe exchanging an external IdP or workload identity token for this credential.

ip_restriction.boundary: Product IP allowlists block programmatic API access in general, but exempt several OAuth types (TwoLeggedOAuth application links, Forge 2LO/3LO, OAuth 2.0 3LO apps). The docs do not say whether service-account client-credentials tokens are covered or exempt. Allowlists need Premium/Enterprise plans.

renewal.summary: No refresh token is described; the script requests a new access token with the client ID and secret. The page does not state whether the client secret itself expires.

administration.summary: Organization admins create service accounts and their OAuth credentials in Atlassian Administration (Directory > Service accounts). Credentials use scopes, selectable only for Jira, Confluence, Goals and Projects. Revoking a credential removes it permanently; deleting the service account removes its credentials.
administration.conditions: Requires the centralized user management experience. Works with Confluence Cloud, Jira Cloud and Jira Align REST APIs via api.atlassian.com. Five service accounts per organization are free; more need Atlassian Guard. Not available on Atlassian Government Cloud.

offboard.details: Service accounts are not tied to a person.
